newsitem.title: USA: Indiana Gov calls special budget session Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Indiana Gov calls special budget session Wednesday.

text.p: Indiana Gov. Frank O'Bannon has called a special budget session for Wednesday afternoon to try to resolve the legislative impasse over the two-year spending package.
Legislators in late April failed to reach an accord on the approximately $16.8 billion general fund budget for fiscal 1998-99.
The resulting deadlock stalled legislation for financing a new Indiana Pacers arena and ultimately O'Bannon vetoed tax bills for financing an Indianapolis convention center expansion.
Lt. Gov. Joe Kernan said Tuesday that state officials hope to get an agreement and finish the budget and other remaining bills in a one-day session.
"I don't think we are really going to know until tommorrow afternoon," Kernan said.
O'Bannon had set a special session for June 2, but said he could move it up if necessary.
